validity.researcher_notes: Phase IV is a real, well-documented FERC Natural Gas Act Sec. 7 certificate project, Docket No. CP99-94-000 -- not a duplicate/relabel of any sibling FGT phase and not a phantom entry. Existence + classification independently confirmed by TWO separate origins: (1) the Florida Gas/Enron/Citrus/Southern Union corporate family's own SEC filings (Enron 2000 10-K; Enron 2004 bankruptcy Disclosure Statement Exhibit 99.12; Southern Union 2005 10-K; Citrus Corp 2011 10-K exhibit -- all describing the same underlying facts, so treated as ONE origin under the independence doctrine for the numeric figures), and (2) a genuinely independent federal source -- the FERC's own Notice of Availability of the Final EIS for the FGT Phase IV Expansion Project, published in the Federal Register Feb 3, 2000 under Docket No. CP99-94-000 -- plus (3) an independent third-party customer document, Progress Energy Florida's Jan 2005 transportation-services exhibit, which references 'FGT's Phase IV Expansion' replacement service agreement (dated June 14, 1999, amended Oct 11, 2000) entirely outside the FGT corporate family. GEM's existing values check out closely: Length 139.00mi vs sourced 139.5mi (Enron ex99-12) -- INDEPENDENTLY corroborated by the FERC/Federal Register FEIS notice, which itemizes the actual facilities (9.3mi 36-in MS Mainline Loop + 6.1mi 30-in FL Bradford Loop + 4.57mi 12-in Sarasota Lateral Loop + 0.84mi 6-in Lake Wales Lateral Loop Ext + 5.73mi 4-in Tampa South Lateral Ext + 75.3mi 30-in + 37.7mi 26-in West Leg Extension), which sum to 139.54mi -- a real match from a source with zero corporate-family relationship to Enron/FGT (tier=high). Capacity 200.00 MMcf/d matches the Enron 2000 10-K's own rounded figure ('approximately 200 MMcf per day'); ex99-12 gives the more precise 196,405 MMBtu/d -- same corporate family for both, so tier=medium despite exhaustive search (FERC docket order text itself was not independently retrievable; elibrary.ferc.gov is a JS SPA with no scriptable text export). SegmentCost 262,000,000 USD is an EXACT match to ex99-12's 'estimated project costs of $262 million' (note: actual total costs through Dec 31, 2002 were $244 million per the same filing; Enron's own 10-K rounds this differently to ~$250 million) -- tier=medium, single corporate family. StartYear1=2001 confirmed exact ('placed in service on May 1, 2001', ex99-12; 'scheduled to go in service in May 2001', Enron 10-K) -- both same corporate family, tier=medium. A genuine SPEC finding: GEM's Diameter value '30, 36 in' captures only the two largest mainline-loop segments; the FERC/FedReg FEIS notice shows Phase IV actually used SIX distinct diameters across its component facilities (4, 6, 12, 26, 30, and 36 in) -- flagged separately below as a spec concern, not fixed here since GEM's convention may intend 'primary trunk diameters only.' No source found for Pressure or a specific Construction start date despite search; left UNRESOLVED. Also found: this pipeline's Docket No. is CP99-94-000, and the underlying Feb 1999 application was originally larger (205mi/272,000 MMBtu-d/$351M est.) before an Aug 23, 1999 amendment (also independently confirmed by the FERC FEIS notice) cut it to the final 139.5mi/196,405 MMBtu-d/$262M version GEM's numbers reflect -- worth noting for anyone reconciling against an early-vintage source that might still show the larger pre-amendment figures.

cross_row_leads.facts: Enron's 2004 bankruptcy Disclosure Statement Exhibit 99.12 describes Florida Gas's 'Phase V Expansion' as ONE project (not yet broken into the sheet's Stages 1-2/3/4 split): 'In April 2003, Florida Gas completed its Phase V Expansion, which added approximately 167 miles of pipeline and approximately 133,000 hp of additional compression. The Phase V Expansion increased the Florida Gas pipeline system's capacity by approximately 428 BBtu/d.' Cost: 'Total estimated costs for the project are $425 million.' In-service timeline: 'Portions of the project were placed in service from December 2001 through December 2002, with the remainder of the Phase V Expansion placed in service in April 2003' (first stage in-service April 2002 per a separate passage on the Mobile Bay lateral acquisition). FERC order approving Phase V issued July 27, 2001, accepted by Florida Gas August 7, 2001. NOTE: these are AGGREGATE figures for the whole Phase V Expansion, not disaggregated by the sheet's Stage 1-2/3/4 split -- not a valid direct fill for any one stage-level cell per the aggregate-vs-segment rule, but a strong lead for whoever researches P4037 (and siblings P4036 'Phase V Stage 3', P4035 'Phase V Stage 4') to reconcile stage-by-stage mileage/capacity/cost against this $425M/167mi/428 BBtu-d total. Earlier, less precise estimate from Enron's FY2000 10-K (filed 2001, before Phase V was finalized): 'preliminary approvals from the FERC for its Phase V expansion, which will increase capacity an additional approximately 400 MMcf per day at an estimated cost of $420 million... expected to be in service in 2002' -- useful as a documented earlier/superseded estimate if any sibling row's current sourcing still reflects pre-2001 numbers.

The same Enron Exhibit 99.12 describes Florida Gas's 'Phase VI Expansion' (docket CP02-27-000, application filed Nov 15, 2001): 'Florida Gas is in the process of constructing approximately 33 miles of pipeline and approximately 18,600 hp of additional compression at existing compression stations, which will increase its summer capacity by approximately 121 BBtu/d... estimated to cost approximately $100 million.' Certificate approved June 13, 2002 (following an environmental order Feb 28, 2002); 'the initial stage of its Phase VI Expansion was placed in service on June 1, 2003, and, except for certain compression modifications, the remainder of the project was completed on November 1, 2003.' A rehearing request on the environmental conditions was denied by FERC order Sept 3, 2002. This looks like a strong, precise, single-project match for P4034 ('Phase VI Project') -- 33mi/18,600hp/121 BBtu-d/$100M/in-service June-Nov 2003 -- worth checking against P4034's current sheet values.
